title: Free Energy Mixer
claim: Standard reads collapse stored items into one convex average, blocking per-channel selection; a value-tilted free-energy read enables it, and common fixes fall short.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right; (a) problem, (b) method, (c) fix comparison list
description: Three vertical panels separated by dashed lines. Panel (a) shows standard attention. A green Query vector and a row of purple Keys feed a bell-curve selection distribution. That distribution is combined over a grid of cached Values, drawn as yellow columns of colored shapes, to give one averaged output column. Below it, red boxes mark per-channel argmax picks scattered across the columns, with a red question mark showing this can't be represented. Panel (b) shows the FEM flow: query, keys and a red temperature vector produce a prior distribution, which is then tilted per channel into several sharp blue posteriors over the value columns. Yellow arrows mark the evidence and update steps. Panel (c) opens with the FEM formula, then lists four existing fixes (more heads, deeper layers, more complexity, other multi-dimensional selection), each with small icon diagrams and short notes on why it fails.
caption: (a) Classic attention stores past values losslessly but reads them as a single convex combination, so channel-wise indexing (e.g., per-channel argmax) is not representable. (b) Free Energy Mixer (FEM) treats selection as a DV free-energy problem: values tilt the prior to a value-aware posterior with a learnable per-channel temperature, enabling low-entropy (point-like) posteriors and channel-wise selection while preserving the prior’s time complexity. (c) Common fixes (more heads, deeper stacks, separable mixers, and per-channel scoring) either keep channels synchronized or raise cost / rely on fixed-state storage; none close the lossy-memory gap that FEM addresses.
abstract: Standard attention stores keys/values losslessly but reads them via a per-head convex average, blocking channel-wise selection. We propose the Free Energy Mixer (FEM): a free-energy (log-sum-exp) read that applies a value-driven, per-channel log-linear tilt to a fast prior (e.g., from queries/keys in standard attention) over indices. Unlike methods that attempt to improve and enrich the $(q,k)$ scoring distribution, FEM treats it as a prior and yields a value-aware posterior read at unchanged complexity, smoothly moving from averaging to per-channel selection as the learnable inverse temperature increases, while still preserving parallelism and the original asymptotic complexity ($O(T^2)$ for softmax; $O(T)$ for linearizable variants). We instantiate a two-level gated FEM that is plug-and-play with standard and linear attention, linear RNNs and SSMs. It consistently outperforms strong baselines on NLP, vision, and time-series at matched parameter budgets.
